In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence of a cost–quality relationship in this study.
the relationship between cost reductions and quality improvements depends on the location of a hospital within the cost × 4-quadrant framework.
there is no evidence of a trade-off between cost of care and quality of care in Korea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cost–quality relationship is not a simple trade-off but is a more complicated relationship that depends on the location of hospitals in the 4 quadrants and that the cost and quality performances are positively associated with each other.
the cost–quality relationship is not a linear trade-off.
the hospitals with higher cost did not necessarily have higher quality, and the same was true of the hospitals with lower cost.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cost–quality trade-offs are not inevitable.
the relationship between cost reduction and quality improvement may not be as straightforward as expected.
cost and quality may not be trade-off in the Korean context, and that cost reduction should not be the only policy priority.
